source_refs.note: Topic 6.4.1.1 Core Principles (PDF 162-163, printed 159-160). The book says consensus needs a 'unanimous decision'; it needs a sufficient majority (general knowledge, flagged). MCQ 13 and short question 2 are answered. Recorded.

items: Decentralization: a network of computers (nodes) maintains the blockchain instead of a central authority, reducing the risk of a single point of failure.
Immutability: once a block is added it cannot be altered or deleted, so the transaction history is permanent and tamper-proof.
Consensus mechanisms: rules such as Proof of Work (PoW) and Proof of Stake (PoS) by which nodes agree that transactions are valid before a block is added.

blocks.text: The book says consensus requires a unanimous decision of all nodes. In practice these mechanisms need agreement from enough of the network, a majority of computing power or stake, not every node.

blocks.prompt: Describe immutability in blockchain and why it is critical (short question 2). Which best describes immutability (MCQ 13)?
blocks.explanation: (c) data being unalterable once added. Each block holds the previous block's hash, and every node keeps a copy, so changing an old record would break the links and disagree with all other copies. This makes the history permanent and trustworthy, which is vital for money, contracts, certificates and supply records.
